h.strategy: Before proposing, briefly model the system: which components carry most of the signal, which are redundant, and where saturation, bottlenecks or substitution between components could occur. Then propose hypotheses that each test a DIFFERENT mechanism (e.g., redundancy, saturation/diminishing returns, bottleneck, interference, compensation, sign reversal). Prefer interactions where the intuitive answer is plausibly wrong, including cases where a usually helpful edit should help LESS or even hurt. Use varied edit fields, condition fields and both directions; no two hypotheses may share the same edit-condition pair or the same underlying reason. Each 'why' must name a concrete mechanism and what pattern would falsify it, not just say a component 'matters more'.

hyps.why: With the direct edge 3 removed, edge 5 is a main route to the output so a 3x3 conv there matters more.
With edge 5 none the output has fewer routes, so a skip on edge 3 restores connectivity and gradient flow.
Replacing none with skip adds a new shortcut path, gaining more than replacing an existing op.
A strong conv already feeding the output via edge 4 makes an extra conv on edge 3 partly redundant.
With edge 5 already a 3x3 conv into the output, a parallel conv on edge 4 adds little.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on the entry edge loses capacity, whereas other starting ops (notably none) make skip a gain.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with skip discards capacity, unlike replacing none, which adds a path.
Turning an absent edge into a conv adds a new parallel path to node 2, beating an op swap on an existing edge.
Without the direct shortcut, edge 0 is on the sole trunk to the output so improving it matters more.
Replacing none on edge 0 revives node 1 and the whole downstream branch.
